brief: A caddy that holds two jerry cans of petrol upright in the boot of my car.

requirements.requirement: Caddy holds two jerry cans upright
requirements.evidence: Two adjacent full-hex bins (bin:0,0,1~hex-bin-full and bin:0,1,1~hex-bin-full) on 2-storey 2x2 base (8x bases + caps + jointBolts). Each bin is full-depth pocket (~176x153mm interior, 80mm deep on top of 80mm lower storey walls) providing upright containment walls on all sides to prevent tipping/sliding; separate compartments keep cans upright and separated.

requirements.requirement: Sized to fit in the boot of a car (compact, stable, low)
requirements.evidence: Measured build 364mm x 467mm x 169mm tall – fits typical car boot footprint. Low-walled double-height frame with closed side caps and locked joints for sliding resistance in transit.

requirements.requirement: Secure retention safe for petrol transport
requirements.evidence: Shape provides upright retention and separation; however configurator cannot verify material fuel-compatibility, strength, sealing or ventilation. Parts are 3D-printed in user-chosen filament – no petrol resistance/heat certification. User must use sealed approved cans, ensure ventilation and strap/secure caddy per local regulations.

finish.summary: 2-bay upright caddy: 4-base footprint, 2 storeys high (169mm) with two full-depth hex bins as dedicated jerry-can pockets. Capped and joint-locked for boot use. Geometry secures cans upright; no fuel prop available to show cans – fuel safety must be handled by approved sealed cans and user material choice.

lines.label: Edge cap · male, two stories tall
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.

events.text:
A compact caddy sized for a car boot (~364 x 467mm footprint, 169mm tall) with two independent deep pockets that each hold a standard 5/10L Jerry can upright and prevent tipping/sliding.

**We checked**: No `jerry-can` / `fuel` prop exists in the configurator catalogue, so cans cannot be shown visually. Dressing was kept clear so the two pockets are visible.

**Safety note the configurator requires**: Hex-Cluster parts are 3D-printed in user-chosen filament. The configurator does not verify material, strength, fuel-compatibility, sealing, ventilation or heat resistance. This shape helps with upright storage and separation, but **do not treat it as certified fuel-safe** — ensure cans are sealed, upright, ventilated, secured in the boot, and compliant with local fuel-transport law. DIY printed plastic is not guaranteed petrol-resistant.
